name: "SLS Nylon PA12",
featuredImage: "v1662650032/gallery/New%20images/Revised/SLS_PA12.jpg",
descriptionShort: "Nylon PA12 (Polyamide) is a strong and heat-resistant material commonly used to print strong and functional parts.",
description: "Nylon PA12 (Polyamide) is a fantastic all-round material with high precision that is also good value for money. When thin, it is flexible enough for springs – when thick, it is strong enough for functional parts. Thanks to that strength and flexibility, it is extremely versatile and suitable for many varied applications. It comes in a variety of colors, and its surface can be polished and dyed. This material is 3D printed on industrial grade 3D printers for the highest quality, using a process called Selective Laser Sintering. PA12 absorbs less water than PA6, but PA6 is stronger than PA12.",

description: "Sandblasted SLS nylon PA12 features a matte, uniform surface achieved through fine abrasive blasting. This process removes excess powder residue and smooths the slightly rough texture inherent to SLS prints, resulting in a refined and consistent appearance. While the finish improves the part’s visual appeal and surface feel, it does not significantly alter dimensional accuracy or mechanical properties. {
id: "612e33ca-b17a-5e87-b86b-6f42b8badd03",
name: "Dyed Velvet",
featuredImage: "v1661938270/gallery/New%20images/SLS_PA12_velvet.jpg",
description: "The process of adding a velvet finish to your models is called flocking. First, a suitable adhesive is applied to the surface. Then, the flock is applied, penetrating the surface of the adhesive to create the desired velvet finish. It not only changes the way your model looks but also how it feels. Electrostatic flock applicators charge the flock particles, which are then attracted to the grounded surface they are attached to. The electrostatic charge ensures that all fibers end up standing at right angles to the surface, resulting in a velvet finish. Velvet fur is fairly resistant to friction.",
descriptionShort: "Dyed SLS Nylon PA12 with a soft and furry finish.",

id: "fbedc6be-7917-4703-83b4-eb4be46e6dbc",
name: "Cerakote Ceramic Coating",
featuredImage: "v1763482458/gallery/Cerakote_Green.jpg",
description: "Cerakote Ceramic Coating applied to SLS Nylon 12 creates a thin, uniform matte surface that significantly enhances the part’s durability and appearance. This advanced ceramic-based coating improves abrasion resistance, UV stability, and chemical protection while maintaining the dimensional accuracy of the underlying printed component. The process results in a refined, professional finish that conceals the rough texture of as-printed SLS Nylon, transforming it into a smooth and visually consistent surface. Cerakote is also available in a wide range of colors, allowing for both aesthetic customization and functional performance. Ideal for end-use parts, housings, and mechanical components, this finish adds long-term protection against environmental wear without compromising the lightweight strength and flexibility of Nylon 12.",
descriptionShort: "Cerakote-coated SLS Nylon 12 parts feature a thin, durable ceramic layer that enhances surface hardness, wear resistance, and color uniformity. The coating provides a premium matte finish with improved UV and chemical protection.",

descriptionShort: "Developed by HP, MJF Nylon is a widely used material for strong and detailed end-use parts and prototypes.",
description: "HP’s Multi Jet Fusion technology is a new printing process that uses special fusing and detailing agents in combination with heat lamps to fuse particles in a bed of powder. Each new layer is fused to the last in order to produce parts with a tensile strength in the Z-axis that is comparable to that in the XY-plane. Resulting models have excellent mechanical properties, with a strength and density exceeding that of parts produced using other powder-based technologies. The strength and heat resistance makes it an excellent choice for functional parts, such as components for drones, mounts, and gears. Thin walls are flexible, which makes nylon great for living hinges and compliant mechanisms. The surface can be post-processed to be smooth and semi-glossy, which makes this material great for visual prototypes and home decor.",

{
id: "ab725db9-80af-5bfd-a07a-bcebaf8676bd",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",
descriptionShort: "A smooth, glossy surface achieved through mechanical tumbling, enhancing aesthetics and reducing surface roughness on MJF PA12 parts.",

description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. featuredImage: "v1704704444/gallery/SHOT_PEENING_PRODUCT_PHOTO.jpg",
description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the nylon's surface. This process smooths the rough texture typical of 3D prints and introduces compressive stress, enhancing the model's resistance to fatigue and cracks. It improves both the aesthetic and functional durability of the models, making them smoother and more resilient.",
descriptionShort: "Shot peening improves both the aesthetic and functional durability of the models, making them smoother and more resilient.",

description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. description: "HP® 3D HR PA 12 is an industrial-grade nylon powder designed for Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 3D printing. It offers excellent strength, durability, and dimensional stability across complex geometries. The material delivers consistent mechanical properties, good chemical resistance, and wear performance, making it suitable for both functional prototypes and end-use parts. Common applications include housings, jigs and fixtures, automotive components, consumer products, and industrial tooling. Its versatility allows for parts that endure repeated handling or moderate mechanical loads.",

description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. The surface is first prepared to ensure proper adhesion, then immersed in a plating solution where an electrical current causes metal ions to bond to the surface. This creates a smooth, metallic finish that not only improves functionality but also provides a sleek, visually appealing look, making it suitable for a range of industrial uses.",
descriptionShort: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity.",

id: "ae761ce9-c041-4e7f-b272-fe960a790063",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",
descriptionShort: "A smooth, glossy surface achieved through mechanical tumbling, enhancing aesthetics and reducing surface roughness on MJF PA12 parts.",

name: "Shot Peened",
featuredImage: "v1710236859/gallery/MJF_PA12_Grey_Shot_Peened.png",
description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. This process smooths the rough texture typical of 3D prints and introduces compressive stress, enhancing the model's resistance to fatigue and cracks. description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",

name: "Shot Peened",
featuredImage: "v1710236859/gallery/MJF_PA12_Grey_Shot_Peened.png",
description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. This process smooths the rough texture typical of 3D prints and introduces compressive stress, enhancing the model's resistance to fatigue and cracks. description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. The surface is first prepared to ensure proper adhesion, then immersed in a plating solution where an electrical current causes metal ions to bond to the surface. This creates a smooth, metallic finish that not only improves functionality but also provides a sleek, visually appealing look, making it suitable for a range of industrial uses.",
descriptionShort: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity.",

featuredImage: "v1755681340/gallery/UV_Powder_Coating_red.jpg",
description: "This UV powder coating finish delivers a uniform, high-quality surface for HP® 3D HR PA 12 S parts, enabled by Arkema. It preserves the dimensional accuracy of 3D printed parts while adding a professional, visually appealing finish. Ideal for functional prototypes, industrial components, and end-use products where aesthetics, durability, and environmental resistance are important.",

name: "HP® MJF PA12 Flame Retardant",
featuredImage: "v1751898292/gallery/HP_3D_HR_PA_12_FR_transparent.png",
descriptionShort: "Developed by HP and Evonik, MJF PA12 Flame Retardant is ideal for functional parts to be used in industrial and electrical applications.",
description: "HP® MJF PA12 Flame Retardant is designed for parts that need to be both tough and fire-safe. It’s halogen-free and certified to meet strict flammability standards, making it a great choice for applications in electronics, transportation, and industrial environments. Whether it’s protective housings, connectors, or interior components, PA12 FR delivers reliable strength and crisp detail without the need for metal.

This material is also well-suited for replacing traditional CNC-machined parts, offering similar durability with significantly reduced weight and faster turnaround times. Its smooth surface finish makes it ideal for end-use parts, and it’s compatible with advanced finishing techniques like vapor smoothing.

On top of performance, it’s produced with a focus on sustainability, using renewable energy and enabling powder reuse to reduce waste. If you need functional parts that are fire-safe, lightweight, and look great right off the printer, PA12 FR is a smart and efficient choice.",

descriptionShort: "Nylon PA6 is a strong and heat-resistant material commonly used to print strong and functional parts.",
description: "Nylon (polyamide PA) is a fantastic all-round material with high precision and a good value for money. Thanks to its strength and flexibility it is extremely versatile and suitable for functional parts, jewelry, and many more applications. When thin, it is flexible enough for springs – when thick, it is strong enough for functional parts. It comes in many colors, and its surface can be polished and dyed. This material is 3D printed on industrial grade 3D printers, offering the highest quality, using a process called Selective Laser Sintering. PA6 is stronger than PA12, but absorbs more water.",

{
id: "b6745bc6-e2a4-4044-b0b8-8cc507f97b4e",
name: "Electroplated",
featuredImage: "v1728543624/gallery/Electroplated_Gold_MJF_large.jpg",
description: "Electroplating on MJF PA 11 involves applying a thin metal layer over the nylon surface to improve performance and aesthetics. Since PA 11 is porous and non-conductive, the part is first smoothed and sealed, then coated with a conductive seed layer to ensure proper adhesion. The component is immersed in a plating solution, where an electrical current bonds metal ions to the surface, creating a uniform metallic layer. This process improves durability, surface hardness, and corrosion resistance, while also enabling electrical conductivity where required. Beyond functionality, the finish provides a refined metallic appearance, making electroplated PA 11 suitable for both industrial applications and decorative uses.",
descriptionShort: "Electroplated MJF PA 11 parts feature a thin metal coating that enhances durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity while giving the nylon base a smooth, metallic finish.",

{
id: "1abd590e-7761-4dc2-9e2d-faa76708165d",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "Polishing MJF PA 11 parts creates a smoother and more uniform surface by mechanically or chemically refining the naturally grainy texture of as-printed nylon. This process reduces visible layer lines and improves the tactile quality, giving the part a sleek, professional look while maintaining the mechanical properties of PA 11, such as toughness, ductility, and impact resistance. The polished finish also helps limit surface porosity, which can make the parts easier to clean and more resistant to dirt absorption. With its combination of durability and improved aesthetics, polished PA 11 is ideal for functional prototypes, end-use components, and consumer products where both performance and visual appeal are important.",
descriptionShort: "Polished PA 11 parts feature a smooth, refined surface with reduced graininess compared to standard prints. The process enhances appearance and touch while retaining the material’s toughness and flexibility.",

{
id: "c1ff999a-ac3f-48ea-942d-3291ccd396fe",
name: "Shot Peened",
featuredImage: "v1710236859/gallery/MJF_PA12_Grey_Shot_Peened.png",
description: "Shot peening of MJF PA 11 involves bombarding the printed part’s surface with fine spherical media under controlled conditions. This process compacts the surface, reducing porosity and creating a more uniform matte appearance compared to the rough, grainy texture of as-printed nylon. Beyond aesthetics, shot peening enhances mechanical performance by improving surface density and increasing resistance to fatigue and crack initiation. The resulting parts maintain PA 11’s core properties – toughness, flexibility, and impact resistance – while gaining added durability and a smoother, professional finish. This makes shot peened PA 11 suitable for functional end-use parts, industrial components, and applications where both performance and surface quality are important.",
descriptionShort: "Shot peened PA 11 parts have a denser, smoother surface achieved by blasting fine media against the nylon. The finish improves fatigue resistance, reduces porosity, and gives the part a uniform matte look.",

{
id: "ad59893d-41dc-49be-9562-188b17b93e9b",
name: "Vapor Smoothed",
featuredImage: "v1663945242/gallery/New%20images/Revised/MJF%20PA12%20Vapor%20smoothed.jpg",
description: "Vapor smoothing MJF PA 11 involves exposing the part to a controlled vaporized solvent that partially melts and reflows the outer surface. This treatment seals the naturally porous texture of as-printed nylon, eliminating graininess and creating a smooth, glossy finish. The process not only improves aesthetics but also enhances functionality by reducing moisture absorption, increasing chemical resistance, and making parts easier to clean. Despite the surface transformation, the bulk mechanical properties of PA 11 – toughness, ductility, and impact resistance – remain intact. Vapor smoothed PA 11 is therefore well-suited for end-use components, consumer products, and medical or food-contact applications where a combination of performance, hygiene, and visual appeal is critical.",
descriptionShort: "Vapor smoothed PA 11 parts have a sealed, glossy surface with reduced porosity. The process enhances aesthetics, improves cleanability, and increases resistance to moisture and dirt while maintaining mechanical strength.",

description: "HP® 3D High Reusability PA 12 FR is a flame-retardant polyamide 12 designed for Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 3D printing. It combines the mechanical durability, chemical resistance, and process reliability of standard HP PA 12 with enhanced fire-retardant properties, making it suitable for parts that must meet safety regulations in automotive, electronics, and industrial applications. description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. The surface is first prepared to ensure proper adhesion, then immersed in a plating solution where an electrical current causes metal ions to bond to the surface. This creates a smooth, metallic finish that not only improves functionality but also provides a sleek, visually appealing look, making it suitable for a range of industrial uses.",
descriptionShort: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity.",

id: "e08887aa-6d2c-4aa3-8fd9-74451aaa43f3",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",
descriptionShort: "A smooth, glossy surface achieved through mechanical tumbling, enhancing aesthetics and reducing surface roughness on MJF PA12 parts.",

name: "Shot Peened",
featuredImage: "v1710236859/gallery/MJF_PA12_Grey_Shot_Peened.png",
description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. This process smooths the rough texture typical of 3D prints and introduces compressive stress, enhancing the model's resistance to fatigue and cracks. description: "HP® 3D HR PA 12 W is a versatile, high-performance nylon material optimized for Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) printing. It delivers strong, dimensionally stable parts with excellent impact, fatigue, and chemical resistance, suitable for functional prototypes, end-use components, and assemblies. Its high reusability reduces waste while maintaining consistent part quality, and its natural white color allows for easy post-processing or dyeing. Applications include housings, jigs and fixtures, industrial components, and functional prototypes.",

{
id: "a001c5d2-1935-4bc8-9f1b-19582435bf1e",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",
descriptionShort: "A smooth, glossy surface achieved through mechanical tumbling, enhancing aesthetics and reducing surface roughness on MJF PA12 parts.",

name: "Shot Peened",

description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. description: "HP® 3D High Reusability PA 12 GB is a glass-bead-filled polyamide 12 engineered for Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 3D printing. description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. The surface is first prepared to ensure proper adhesion, then immersed in a plating solution where an electrical current causes metal ions to bond to the surface. This creates a smooth, metallic finish that not only improves functionality but also provides a sleek, visually appealing look, making it suitable for a range of industrial uses.",

name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1661952138/gallery/New%20images/MJF_polished.jpg",
description: "This polished finish is applied to MJF PA12 parts using a mechanical tumbling process, which gently smooths and rounds the surface without affecting the part’s dimensions. Tumbling removes fine layer lines and powder residues from 3D printing, resulting in a glossy, visually appealing surface. The process enhances part aesthetics, improves tactile feel, and reduces friction on contact surfaces, making it suitable for functional prototypes, consumer products, and display models. The mechanical nature of the polishing ensures consistency and preserves dimensional accuracy while improving the overall quality of the printed part.",
descriptionShort: "A smooth, glossy surface achieved through mechanical tumbling, enhancing aesthetics and reducing surface roughness on MJF PA12 parts.",

name: "Shot Peened",
featuredImage: "v1710236859/gallery/MJF_PA12_Grey_Shot_Peened.png",
description: "Shot peening is a technique where tiny shots are blasted at high speed, creating indentations on the Nylon's surface. This process smooths the rough texture typical of 3D prints and introduces compressive stress, enhancing the model's resistance to fatigue and cracks. {
id: "561de701-1136-491b-8dd8-c238f76c6869",
name: "Vapor Smoothed",

descriptionShort: "Nylon PA6 is a durable, wear-resistant thermoplastic with excellent impact strength, low friction, and good machinability. Ideal for precision mechanical components like gears, bushings, and automotive parts.",
description: "Nylon PA6, also known as Polyamide 6, is a versatile, high-performance engineering thermoplastic that excels in applications requiring strength, durability, and resistance to wear and fatigue. It is particularly known for its high impact strength, low friction, and good chemical resistance. With excellent machinability, PA6 is ideal for precision components such as gears, bearings, bushings, and automotive parts. It performs well under moderate loads and provides good dimensional stability over a wide temperature range. Nylon PA6 also offers natural resistance to abrasion and is commonly used in functional prototypes, wearable parts, and components exposed to harsh environments. Its low moisture absorption rate and good electrical insulating properties make it suitable for electrical components and high-performance mechanical systems.",

descriptionShort: "SLS Glass-Filled Nylon PA6 is a glass-fiber-reinforced nylon with exceptional stiffness, heat resistance, and dimensional stability. The material’s matte surface makes it ideal for strong, durable, and thermally stable functional parts.",
description: "SLS Glass-Filled Reinforced Nylon 6 (PA6 GF40) is a high-performance thermoplastic designed for applications that demand superior strength, rigidity, and thermal stability. Containing approximately 40% glass fiber, the material exhibits excellent stiffness and dimensional stability, even under high mechanical loads or elevated temperatures. Printed parts feature a matte finish with a slightly textured surface characteristic of SLS processing. The glass fiber reinforcement significantly reduces warping and shrinkage, ensuring tight tolerances and consistent accuracy. With high heat deflection, chemical resistance, and impact strength, SLS PA6 GF40 is well-suited for industrial applications such as automotive housings, structural brackets, and components exposed to mechanical or thermal stress.",

name: "SLS Nylon PA6 Carbon Fiber",
featuredImage: "v1764249552/PA6_CF_qzorat.png",
descriptionShort: "SLS PA6 Carbon Fiber parts offer high stiffness, excellent dimensional stability, and improved heat resistance. The carbon fiber reinforcement is ideal for strong functional components and demanding engineering applications.",
description: "SLS PA6 Carbon Fiber is a high-performance nylon composite reinforced with carbon fibers to deliver exceptional stiffness, strength, and thermal stability. When produced via Selective Laser Sintering, the material forms dense, highly rigid parts with excellent dimensional accuracy and minimal deformation, making it suitable for demanding mechanical and structural applications. The carbon reinforcement significantly increases tensile modulus and heat resistance compared to unfilled PA6, enabling reliable performance under load, impact, and elevated temperatures.
As printed, PA6 Carbon Fiber parts exhibit a matte black to dark charcoal finish with a fine, uniform SLS texture. The surface shows subtle fiber-reinforced micro-granularity often associated with carbon composite parts, offering both a technical appearance and excellent functional durability. Components benefit from reduced warping, enhanced stiffness-to-weight ratio, and outstanding dimensional stability.
Typical end uses include automotive housings, UAV and robotics components, jigs and fixtures, brackets, enclosures, load-bearing structures, and high-temperature functional prototypes. Overall, SLS PA6 Carbon Fiber combines the robustness of engineering nylon with the performance boost of carbon fiber, making it a top choice for strong, lightweight, end-use parts.",

name: "Standard",
featuredImage: "v1764249552/PA6_CF_qzorat.png",
description: "In its standard, as-printed state, SLS PA6 Carbon Fiber (PA6-CF) produces parts with a matte black to deep charcoal finish and a fine, uniform sintered texture typical of SLS processing. The carbon fiber reinforcement gives the surface a subtle micro-granular composite appearance, adding to the material’s engineered aesthetic and contributing to its exceptional rigidity. Layer lines are virtually invisible due to the powder-based manufacturing process, resulting in clean edges and consistent surfaces ideal for functional engineering environments.
The material offers high tensile strength, very high stiffness, outstanding heat resistance (HDT ~180-200 °C), and excellent dimensional stability. This makes the standard finish suitable for end-use components without the need for post-processing. Although the material is strong and lightweight, it is less ductile than unfilled nylons, so thin or highly flexible features should be engineered carefully.
Typical applications for PA6-CF in its as-printed state include automotive housings, UAV and robotics parts, brackets, tooling, jigs, fixtures, load-bearing structures, and high-temperature functional components. The technical matte surface and robust mechanical behavior make it an ideal choice for performance-driven manufacturing.",
descriptionShort: "As-printed SLS PA6 Carbon Fiber parts feature a matte black, finely textured surface. The carbon reinforcement delivers high strength, heat resistance, and a technical composite look suitable for demanding functional components.",

featuredImage: "v1661937989/gallery/New%20images/FDM_Sanded.jpg",
description: "Flat surfaces, curves and overhangs are smoothed out with specific tools or by manually sanding them to the extent that layer lines are less visible. The color might be slightly uneven due to the sanding. PLA is short for Polylactic Acid, a thermoplastic polymer that is derived from renewable resources. This feature sets it apart from other commonly used plastics. PLA material is great for low cost prototyping, low-wear toys, functional parts under light load, and containers. The printing process - An extruder deposits molten plastic onto a build platform, layer by layer, until the model has been created. The printing process creates visible stepping between layers. The infill percentage can be customized to your needs in the "Finish" step of our configuration.",
descriptionShort: "Smooth sanded finish in various colors.",

descriptionShort: "ABS is a durable and versatile material with good impact and chemical resistance. It is great for functional parts and prototypes.",
description: "ABS (acrylonitrile butadiene styrene) is great for functional parts and prototypes with a need for stronger mechanical properties than PLA. ABS matches approximately 80% of the properties of injection-molded products but is rigid and inflexible, with design freedom limited due to the fused deposition modeling (FDM) printing process. The surface of an ABS model is always slightly rough due to the printing process and it can be difficult to post-process, though vapor smoothing can greatly improve its aspect.",

descriptionShort: "PLA+ and Tough PLA offer enhanced strength and durability compared to regular PLA, ideal for functional prototypes and mechanical parts.",
description: "PLA+ and Tough PLA represent advancements over traditional PLA filament, offering enhanced mechanical properties without compromising on ease of use and eco-friendliness. Both PLA variants provide improved impact resistance, less brittleness, reduced warping, minimal deformation and better layer adhesion compared to regular PLA. name: "PCTG",
featuredImage: "v1685518371/gallery/pctg_black.jpg",
descriptionShort: "PCTG is a thermoplastic polyester that offers a good balance of strength, durability, chemical resistance, and food safety compliance. Its good mechanical properties make it suitable for a wide range of functional and aesthetic applications.",
description: "PCTG (Poly – Cyclohexylenedimethylene Terephthalate Glycol) is a thermoplastic polyester that offers a good balance of strength, durability, chemical resistance, and food safety compliance. Its ease of printing and good mechanical properties make it suitable for a wide range of functional and aesthetic applications.
One of the significant advantages of PCTG filament is its compliance with FDA regulations for food contact. It is considered food-safe and can be used to print objects that come into contact with food and beverages. Please be aware that while the material is food-safe, the FDM printing process is not.
PCTG has a low tendency to warp or shrink during the printing process, making it easier to achieve accurate and consistent prints.
It exhibits excellent mechanical properties, including high tensile strength and impact resistance, which makes it suitable for functional prints that require strength and durability.
It further has good chemical resistance, making it resistant to a wide range of chemicals, oils, and solvents.
PCTG has a lower glass transition temperature (Tg) compared to materials like ABS or Polycarbonate, limiting its use in high-temperature environments.",

featuredImage: "v1737646567/pmma_transparent_01_revised_e21okn.jpg",
descriptionShort: "Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA), commonly known as acrylic or plexiglass, offers optical clarity and excellent mechanical properties, such as high tensile strength and impact resistance. Additionally it provides chemical- and UV-resistance.",
description: "Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA), commonly known as acrylic or plexiglass, offers good optical clarity, which makes it ideal for applications where visual aesthetics and light transmission are paramount, such as display cases, signage, or architectural models.

In addition to its optical properties, PMMA exhibits excellent mechanical characteristics. It possesses high tensile strength and impact resistance, making it stronger and more durable than materials like PLA or ABS. This strength enables PMMA to withstand demanding conditions and endure impacts without compromising its integrity.

One of the notable advantages of PMMA is its resistance to chemicals. It demonstrates good resistance to various substances, including acids and alkalis.

PMMA also excels in its resistance to ultraviolet (UV) light degradation. It maintains its clarity and mechanical properties when exposed to sunlight or other UV sources, making it a preferred choice for outdoor applications.",

name: "PETG-HT",
featuredImage: "v1687776219/PETG_HT_2_vivjay.jpg",
descriptionShort: "PETG-HT is an enhanced version of PETG, specifically designed to withstand high temperatures and exhibit excellent mechanical properties.",
description: "PETG-HT is engineered to have an increased glass transition temperature (Tg), which is the temperature at which the material transitions from a rigid to a soft and pliable state. This enhanced formulation allows it to withstand higher heat environments compared to standard PETG filament.

The higher Tg of PETG-HT makes it suitable for applications where exposure to elevated temperatures is expected, such as functional prototypes, automotive components, mechanical parts, and industrial tooling. It offers improved dimensional stability, reduced warping, and enhanced resistance to heat deformation compared to regular PETG filament.

PETG-HT retains many of the desirable properties of PETG, including good layer adhesion, low shrinkage, and resistance to chemicals, making it a reliable choice for a wide range of 3D printing applications.",

descriptionShort: "316L Stainless Steel printed with Metal Binder Jetting technology.",
description: "Metal Binder Jetting (MBJ) printed 316L stainless steel combines the inherent strengths of 316L stainless steel with the unique capabilities of MBJ technology. 316L  is known for its excellent corrosion resistance, making it ideal for harsh environments. The MBJ technology can create complex geometries with more design freedom than traditional manufacturing methods. The MBJ printed parts have good mechanical properties, yet they do not match the density and strength of parts made through methods like DMLS/SLM. The surface finish of MBJ printed parts is not as smooth as with other methods. Still, MBJ-printed 316L steel is a robust choice for applications needing a balance of corrosion resistance, strength, and complex geometries.",

name: "BASF® Ultrafuse 316L Steel",
featuredImage: "v1663168478/gallery/New%20images/Ultrafuse_316L.jpg",
descriptionShort: "Sintered, FDM printed stainless steel is used for strong and functional parts.",
description: "This is a new industrial-grade metal filament for professional uses. Created by BASF, Ultrafuse 316L filament is composed of 90% stainless steel and 10% polymer binder which allows it to be used in FDM printers. The material is characterized by its impressive mechanical properties and low cost of production, making it one of the most affordable materials for metal 3D printing. The printed part is in a "green state" and must undergo a debinding process to remove the polymer binding agent. After debinding, the part is relatively porous and requires a sintering process to produce a solid, dense part. While the sintered part is ready for use, additional post-processing is possible to create the desired surface quality with polishing, milling, heat-treatment, or coating. Ultrafuse steel has a similar tensile strength but lower yield strength compared to DMLS printed steel.",

description: "The MoldJet® technology involves a mold from a liquid photopolymer, which is then filled with 316L steel powder. After the powder is deposited, the mold is cured and the metal is sintered, resulting in a solid metal part. descriptionShort: "Sintered, FDM printed stainless steel is used for strong and functional parts.",
description: "Ultrafuse stainless steel 17-4 PH is a new industrial-grade metal filament for professional uses. Created by BASF, Ultrafuse 17-4 PH filament is composed of 90% stainless steel and 10% polymer binder which allows it to be used in FDM printers. The material is characterized by its impressive mechanical properties and low cost of production, making it one of the most affordable materials for metal 3D printing. The printed part is in a "green state" and must undergo a debinding process to remove the polymer binding agent. After debinding, the part is relatively porous and requires a sintering process to produce a solid, dense part. While the sintered part is ready for use, additional post-processing is possible to create the desired surface quality with polishing, milling, heat-treatment, or coating. Ultrafuse steel has a similar tensile strength but lower yield strength compared to DMLS printed steel.",

name: "Satin Glossy",
featuredImage: "v1756823852/gallery/glossy_satin_316L_stainless_steel.png",
description: "In a satin glossy finish, CNC machined 316L stainless steel achieves a refined surface that balances a soft brushed texture with a subtle reflective sheen. This glossy satin finish is achieved through a combination of precision machining and controlled surface refinement. After milling or turning, the part is treated with fine abrasive polishing or brushing that smooths tool marks while leaving a subtle directional texture, creating a soft sheen that balances reflectivity with a refined matte look.
This finish reduces the stark mirror effect of a polished surface while still providing a premium, high-quality appearance. It enhances the material’s natural corrosion resistance and durability, making it suitable for both functional components and aesthetic applications. Satin glossy 316L steel is often chosen for consumer products, medical devices, and industrial parts where both performance and a sophisticated visual appeal are required. The finish also improves handling by reducing fingerprint visibility compared to a full mirror polish.",
descriptionShort: "CNC machined 316L stainless steel with a satin glossy finish has a smooth, reflective surface with a fine brushed texture. It combines durability, corrosion resistance, and a premium aesthetic for functional and decorative parts.",

descriptionShort: "Steel 1215 produces highly precise parts with excellent machinability and a smooth surface finish. It offers moderate strength and is ideal for high-volume production of detailed components where tight tolerances and cost efficiency are priorities.",
description: "CNC machined Steel 1215 is a free-machining low-carbon steel specifically designed for high-speed machining and precision manufacturing. Known for its exceptional machinability, the material allows for efficient production, excellent surface finish quality, and reliable dimensional accuracy, making it well suited for high-volume and complex CNC-machined components.

The material’s high sulfur content improves chip breaking and reduces tool wear, enabling faster machining speeds and consistent results. Parts produced in Steel 1215 typically exhibit a clean, uniform metallic appearance with fine machining marks and sharp, well-defined features that support tight tolerances and repeatable performance.

Steel 1215 provides moderate strength and hardness but lower ductility and weldability compared to other carbon steels. It offers limited corrosion resistance and is commonly treated with protective coatings such as plating, painting, or black oxide finishing when used in exposed environments.

Typical applications include fasteners, fittings, bushings, shafts, pins, and precision mechanical components where machinability, cost efficiency, and dimensional accuracy are more important than high structural strength or corrosion resistance.",

description: "In its standard, as-machined state, A36 steel exhibits a matte metallic gray finish with fine tool marks and a slightly rougher texture compared to alloy steels. This finish reflects the raw precision of CNC machining, preserving the natural appearance of structural carbon steel. A36 is a low-carbon steel known for its excellent weldability, ductility, and good mechanical strength, making it suitable for heavy-duty applications such as frames, brackets, and mechanical fixtures. While not as corrosion-resistant as stainless steel, A36 offers excellent machinability and is often coated, painted, or plated for enhanced surface protection. The as-machined finish provides a clean, functional appearance suitable for prototypes, industrial components, or parts intended for post-processing.",

description: "CNC machined O1 tool steel is a high-carbon, oil-hardening tool steel designed for applications requiring excellent hardness, wear resistance, and dimensional stability. Known for its reliable heat treatment response and fine grain structure, O1 tool steel is widely used for precision tooling and mechanical components exposed to friction, stress, or repeated use.

O1 tool steel provides a strong balance of hardness, toughness, and edge retention, allowing components to maintain precise geometry and surface integrity during service. While it offers limited corrosion resistance, protective coatings or controlled environments are typically used when environmental exposure is a concern.

Typical applications include cutting tools, dies, molds, punches, gauges, and wear-resistant machine components where durability, precision, and long service life are essential.",

description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. name: "Electroplated Colored",
featuredImage: "v1754485101/gallery/electroplated_colored.png",
description: "This finish is achieved by electroplating a color-infused metal layer onto the print. It results in a glossy, reflective finish with vibrant, durable colors. The finish enhances both the aesthetic appeal and the functionality of the part, providing increased surface hardness, corrosion resistance, and a unique metallic sheen. This finish is ideal for decorative and functional parts in industries like fashion, art, automotive, and consumer electronics, where both durability and appearance are important.
All colors are mixed to order by our manufacturing partners. 
You can choose the exact hue for your project by providing a hex code in the production notes in your cart.",
descriptionShort: "The finish provides a glossy, metallic appearance with vibrant colors, offering enhanced durability, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appeal for decorative and functional parts.",

description: "This finish is achieved by electroplating a color-infused metal layer onto the print. It results in a glossy, reflective finish with vibrant, durable colors. This finish is ideal for decorative and functional parts in industries like fashion, art, automotive, and consumer electronics, where both durability and appearance are important.
All colors are mixed to order by our manufacturing partners.

Parts printed in VisiJet® M2R-TN feature a tan-colored finish, offering a professional industrial appearance with a matte surface. The material excels in impact resistance and dimensional accuracy, making it suitable for functional prototypes, mechanical components, and low-volume end-use parts. The color adds an aesthetic value while maintaining the high mechanical properties required for real-world applications, particularly in dental mockups, consumer products, and electronics. These parts perform reliably under mechanical stress, ensuring long-lasting durability and precision without the need for post-processing.",

descriptionShort: "Aluminum Alloy 6061 offers excellent strength-to-weight performance, good corrosion resistance, and reliable dimensional stability. It is ideal for lightweight structural parts, prototypes, and functional components requiring durability and machinability.",
description: "Aluminum Alloy 6061 used in Selective Laser Melting (SLM) combines lightweight performance with high strength and good corrosion resistance, making it a versatile material for industrial and engineering applications. In its additively manufactured form, 6061 delivers excellent dimensional accuracy, fine feature detail, and consistent mechanical properties after heat treatment. The alloy maintains strong fatigue resistance, good thermal conductivity, and stable behavior under load, allowing it to be used for functional prototypes, structural components, housings, brackets, and aerospace-grade parts.
Compared to cast or wrought 6061, SLM-produced parts achieve high density and improved geometrical freedom, enabling the creation of lightweight designs that cannot be produced through traditional methods. Post-processing operations such as machining, anodizing, or shot peening are commonly applied to achieve final performance and surface quality. Overall, 6061 for SLM provides an excellent balance of strength, machinability, corrosion resistance, and weight reduction, making it a popular choice for advanced engineering applications.",

description: "In its standard, as-printed state, SLM Aluminum Alloy 6061 exhibits a matte gray finish with a slightly rough texture characteristic of laser-melted aluminum powder. The surface shows fine unmelted granularity and layer-based contouring, which can be smoothed through secondary operations such as machining, shot peening, or bead blasting. Despite the raw surface texture, the material delivers strong mechanical performance, including good tensile strength, fatigue resistance, and corrosion resistance.
SLM 6061 offers excellent dimensional stability and accuracy, making it ideal for functional prototypes, housings, brackets, and lightweight load-bearing structures. However, it is known for high residual stress and warping risk, requiring careful support strategy and post-build heat treatment. The as-printed surface preserves intricate geometries and internal channels while maintaining the alloy’s reliable strength-to-weight ratio. Overall, standard SLM 6061 provides a durable, functional finish suitable for engineering applications where raw surface texture is acceptable or will be post-processed.",
descriptionShort: "Standard SLM Aluminum Alloy 6061 parts feature a matte gray, slightly rough surface with visible powder granularity. The material offers high strength, good corrosion resistance, and excellent dimensional stability.",

{
id: "5b866388-dcc1-4659-ad45-fe706f2f1b2a",
name: "Anodized",
featuredImage: "v1764249525/AL6061_ttxq0n.png",
description: "Anodized SLM Aluminum Alloy 6061 exhibits a uniform matte metallic finish that significantly enhances both functional performance and visual quality. The anodizing process forms a controlled oxide layer that improves corrosion resistance, surface hardness, and abrasion protection, addressing the raw, slightly porous surface typical of as-printed SLM components. Anodizing also helps seal the surface of the part, reducing oxidation and providing a more refined, consistent appearance.
SLM 6061 provides strong mechanical performance, excellent dimensional stability, and low weight, making it suitable for aerospace brackets, housings, fixtures, structural components, and high-precision mechanical parts. Anodizing further improves fatigue resistance and enhances the material’s suitability for demanding environments, including marine, industrial, and outdoor applications. The finish accepts both clear and colored anodizing, allowing for functional marking, aesthetic customization, or enhanced surface durability.
Overall, anodized SLM 6061 combines the geometric freedom of additive manufacturing with the durability and professional appearance of a high-quality metallic finish.",
descriptionShort: "Anodized parts feature a smooth, matte metallic surface with enhanced corrosion resistance, hardness, and wear protection. The finish improves durability and appearance while preserving the material’s structural integrity and lightweight performance.",

{
id: "a7e3fa79-d3c1-495c-905a-1b4758937eb5",
name: "Electrophoresis",
featuredImage: "v1764249525/AL6061_ttxq0n.png",
description: "SLM Aluminum Alloy 6061 with an electrophoresis finish exhibits a smooth, uniform semi-gloss surface that significantly improves both functional performance and visual appeal. Electrophoretic coating (E-coating) creates a thin, consistent polymer layer that enhances corrosion resistance, wear protection, and chemical durability, making it ideal for components exposed to demanding environments. The coating also seals the natural porosity of as-printed SLM 6061, creating a more refined and professional appearance.
This finish is commonly applied in automotive, aerospace, consumer electronics, and industrial equipment, where consistent surface quality and long-term environmental protection are crucial. E-coating adheres extremely well to aluminum, providing stable coverage even in complex geometries produced by SLM. It also offers excellent electrical insulation, improving suitability for housings and enclosures.
Available in various colors – most commonly black, gray, and clear – electrophoresis transforms the raw, textured SLM surface into a smooth, durable, aesthetically enhanced finish while maintaining the alloy’s excellent strength, lightweight performance, and dimensional stability.",
descriptionShort: "Electrophoresis-coated parts feature a smooth, uniform surface with excellent corrosion and wear resistance. The finish provides a durable, semi-gloss appearance while improving environmental protection and overall surface quality.",

id: "c464c345-6aaa-4f38-82e9-cc24f43665a4",
name: "Polished-Ra 3.2",
featuredImage: "v1764249525/AL6061_ttxq0n.png",
description: "Polished SLM Aluminum Alloy 6061 with an Ra 3.2 µm surface finish offers a refined metallic appearance and improved functional performance over the raw, as-printed surface. The polishing process reduces the inherent roughness and powder granularity of SLM printing, producing a smoother, semi-bright surface with visible but softened machining or finishing marks. This finish enhances cleanability, wear resistance, and part handling, making components more suitable for mechanical assemblies, consumer-facing applications, or environments where reduced friction and smoother surfaces are beneficial.
While SLM 6061 maintains excellent strength-to-weight ratio, dimensional accuracy, and corrosion resistance, the Ra 3.2 polish significantly improves tactile quality and visual appeal without removing excessive material or altering geometry. Common applications include structural brackets, enclosures, fixtures, aerospace components, robotics parts, and precision mechanical assemblies where both performance and a refined surface finish are required. The Ra 3.2 polished finish serves as an ideal intermediate step prior to further treatments such as anodizing, electrophoresis, or hard coating.",
descriptionShort: "Polished SLM Aluminum 6061 parts with an Ra 3.2 finish feature a smoother, brighter metallic surface with reduced roughness compared to the as-printed state. This finish improves appearance, cleanability, and functional performance.",

name: "Nickel-Titanium (NiTi)",
featuredImage: "v1732030502/gallery/nitinol.jpg",
descriptionShort: "Nickel-Titanium (NiTi) is a shape memory alloy with superelasticity, fatigue resistance, and biocompatibility. Its phase transformations enable shape recovery after deformation, making it ideal for medical, aerospace, and robotic uses.",
description: "Nickel-Titanium (NiTi) alloy, commonly known as Nitinol, is a highly versatile shape memory alloy with a near-equiatomic composition of nickel and titanium. It is renowned for its unique properties, including shape memory, superelasticity, high fatigue resistance, and biocompatibility. The material undergoes reversible phase transformations, allowing it to recover its original shape after deformation when exposed to specific temperature changes. These characteristics make NiTi ideal for applications requiring flexibility and precision, such as medical implants, actuators, and components in aerospace and robotics. Additionally, NiTi exhibits corrosion resistance and excellent mechanical performance, further enhancing its suitability for demanding environments. Its behavior can be fine-tuned by adjusting composition and thermal treatment, offering adaptability across various industries.",

name: "Anodized",

description: "The anodized finish on CNC-milled Aluminum 6061 creates a hard, matte to satin surface with excellent corrosion and wear resistance. description: "Stainless Steel 15-5 PH is a precipitation-hardened martensitic stainless steel that combines high strength, good toughness, and reliable corrosion resistance with excellent machinability in the solution-treated condition.

Compared with grades like 304 or 316L, 15-5 PH provides significantly higher strength while still maintaining good resistance to atmospheric and mild chemical corrosion.

15-5 PH is commonly used in aerospace, defense, oil and gas, industrial machinery, and high-performance engineering applications, especially where parts must withstand mechanical stress, fatigue, and wear. After machining, the material can be further precipitation hardened to increase strength if required for critical applications.

In its raw as-machined condition, the surface is functional and technical rather than decorative; for outdoor or harsh environments, additional finishing such as passivation, coating, or polishing can further enhance corrosion resistance and appearance.",

descriptionShort: "CNC machined Aluminum 7050 produces very high-strength, lightweight parts with excellent dimensional accuracy and a clean machined surface. It is suited for demanding structural and aerospace applications where maximum performance is required.",
description: "CNC machined Aluminum 7050 is a premium, high-strength aerospace-grade aluminum alloy that delivers exceptional mechanical performance while remaining relatively lightweight and machinable. 

The material offers very high tensile strength, outstanding fatigue resistance, and good fracture toughness, making it one of the best-performing aluminum alloys for load-bearing and safety-critical components. Compared to more common grades like 6061 or 5083, 7050 provides significantly superior structural capability while still allowing tight tolerances, sharp features, and reliable repeatability in machining.

Typical applications include aerospace components, high-performance mechanical parts, structural brackets, precision fixtures, and heavily stressed machine elements. It is especially valued in industries where strength-to-weight ratio and long-term durability under cyclic loads are critical.

In its raw as-machined condition, Aluminum 7050 has limited corrosion resistance compared to some other aluminum alloys, so parts intended for outdoor, marine, or humid environments are often anodized, coated, or painted for protection. Overall, CNC machined Aluminum 7050 is best suited for high-performance, structurally demanding parts where mechanical strength and reliability are prioritized over cosmetic appearance.",

name: "Aluminum MIC-6",
featuredImage: "v1770824531/gallery/CNC_Aluminum_MIC-6.png",
descriptionShort: "CNC machined Aluminum MIC-6 produces dimensionally stable, flat, and precise parts with a clean machined surface. It is ideal for tooling plates, fixtures, and structural components where accuracy and stability are critical.",
description: "Aluminum MIC-6 is a cast, stress-relieved aluminum alloy specifically designed for applications that require exceptional dimensional stability and flatness. Because internal stresses are minimized during production, MIC-6 resists warping and distortion during machining, making it one of the most reliable aluminum grades for precision components and large, machined plates.

The material holds tight tolerances consistently, maintains accurate geometry, and delivers excellent flatness over large surfaces.

MIC-6 is commonly used for machine bases, mounting plates, test fixtures, robotics components, and metrology tooling, where stability and repeatability are more important than maximum strength. While it machines cleanly and predictably, its mechanical strength is lower than high-strength alloys like 2024 or 7050, making it better suited for precision and stability rather than heavily loaded structural parts.

For applications exposed to outdoor or humid environments, additional protection such as anodizing or coating is recommended, as its corrosion resistance is moderate. Aluminum MIC-6 is best suited for high-precision, low-distortion parts where dimensional reliability matters more than ultimate strength or cosmetic appearance.",

descriptionShort: "Sheet metal joining connects metal sheets using welding, riveting, adhesives, or fasteners, essential for creating durable assemblies across industries.",
description: "Sheet metal joining is a manufacturing process that involves connecting metal sheets to create finished products or components. This process is versatile and essential across various industries, including automotive, aerospace, construction, and electronics. Different methods are employed based on the application requirements, such as welding, riveting, adhesive bonding, and mechanical fastening. Welding uses heat to fuse metal sheets, offering strong and permanent joints ideal for automotive and structural applications. Riveting and mechanical fastening provide reliable connections without heat, making them suitable for heat-sensitive applications. Adhesive bonding allows for the joining of dissimilar materials, offering uniform stress distribution. The selection of a joining method depends on factors such as material type, joint strength, and production volume, with modern techniques often combining multiple methods for enhanced performance. Sheet metal joining plays a vital role in creating complex and durable assemblies, supporting a wide range of manufacturing needs.",

featuredImage: "v1715858638/gallery/laser_cutting_Craftcloud_new.jpg",
descriptionShort: "Sheet metal forming shapes metal sheets using techniques like bending and stamping. It's used in automotive, aerospace, and electronics for precise, durable parts.",
description: "Sheet metal forming is a manufacturing process that shapes flat metal sheets into desired geometries using force. This process includes techniques like bending, drawing, stretching, and stamping to create complex parts with precision. It's widely used in industries such as automotive, aerospace, electronics, and construction for its ability to produce lightweight and durable components efficiently.

The process starts with a flat sheet of metal, like aluminum, steel, or copper, which is manipulated using tools and dies. Bending deforms the metal around a straight axis to achieve specific angles. Drawing stretches the metal into a cavity to form cup-like shapes, while stamping cuts and shapes the metal using a press and die to create intricate designs.

Sheet metal forming offers high production speed, cost-effectiveness for large volumes, and the ability to create complex shapes with tight tolerances. The process also allows for significant material conservation, as excess metal can be recycled. Advanced technologies like CAD and CAM have further enhanced the precision and capabilities of sheet metal forming, making it essential in modern manufacturing.",

It is also non-heat-treatable, which means it maintains its strength and durability without requiring additional heat treatment processes.

It provides better hardenability and mechanical performance than lower-alloy steels such as 4130, making it well suited for highly loaded components. While its corrosion resistance is limited, protective coatings or surface treatments can be applied to improve environmental durability.",

name: "Carbon Fiber PPA",
featuredImage: "v1759834077/gallery/CF_PPA_Black.png",
descriptionShort: "Carbon fiber reinforced PPA is a high-performance 3D printable thermoplastic combining excellent stiffness, heat resistance, and chemical stability, ideal for durable functional parts.",
description: "Carbon fiber reinforced PPA (Polyphthalamide) is a high-performance thermoplastic designed for demanding 3D printing applications. By integrating carbon fibers, the material achieves significantly enhanced stiffness, dimensional stability, and mechanical strength while maintaining the inherent chemical and heat resistance of PPA. It performs well in continuous service temperatures up to 200–220 °C and resists exposure to fuels, oils, and industrial chemicals. This combination makes it ideal for automotive, aerospace, industrial machinery, and electrical components, particularly for structural, load-bearing, and high-temperature functional parts. Carbon fiber reinforcement also reduces warping and improves surface flatness, making printed parts more reliable and precise for functional applications.",

description: "Carbon Fiber reinforced PPA (CF-PPA) in its standard, as-printed state exhibits a matte, dark gray to black surface with a slightly rough, textured finish typical of high-performance thermoplastic printing. The carbon fiber reinforcement provides exceptional stiffness and strength, while the PPA base ensures high chemical resistance, thermal stability, and dimensional accuracy. As-printed parts retain these mechanical and chemical properties, making them suitable for demanding functional prototypes, industrial components, and end-use applications in automotive, electronics, and chemical processing industries. The surface texture can help reduce glare and improve handling, while maintaining the robust performance characteristics inherent to CF-PPA.",

Unlike standard ASA, which offers greater impact resistance and flexibility, Glass Fiber ASA provides superior structural integrity and load-bearing capacity, making it ideal for demanding applications.

description: "Electroplating is a process where a thin layer of metal is applied to plastic surfaces to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and electrical conductivity. The surface is first prepared to ensure proper adhesion, then immersed in a plating solution where an electrical current causes metal ions to bond to the surface. This creates a smooth, metallic finish that not only improves functionality but also provides a sleek, visually appealing look, making it suitable for a range of industrial uses.",

featuredImage: "v1754485101/gallery/electroplated_colored.png",
description: "This finish is achieved by electroplating a color-infused metal layer onto the print. It results in a glossy, reflective finish with vibrant, durable colors. The finish enhances both the aesthetic appeal and the functionality of the part, providing increased surface hardness, corrosion resistance, and a unique metallic sheen. This finish is ideal for decorative and functional parts in industries like fashion, art, automotive, and consumer electronics, where both durability and appearance are important.
All colors are mixed to order by our manufacturing partners. 
You can choose the exact hue for your project by providing a hex code in the production notes in your cart.",
descriptionShort: "The finish provides a glossy, metallic appearance with vibrant colors, offering enhanced durability, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appeal for decorative and functional parts.",

descriptionShort: "Polycarbonate is an industrial-grade thermoplastic with high heat resistance and high strength.",
description: "Polycarbonate (PC) is a material renowned in the 3D printing market for its impact resistance and toughness. It is more durable and flexible than PLA but less so than nylon, and it is harder than PLA and PMMA, while also being lighter and less dense than ABS. PC is a lightweight yet strong thermoplastic, ideal for a wide range of professional applications. It is commonly used for phone cases, water bottles, prototype windows, and electronic appliances.",

description: "PVB (Polyvinyl butyral) is known for its excellent adhesion, transparency, and flexibility. Its flexibility and strength make it ideal for creating durable, impact-resistant objects. Common use-cases include protective gear, eyewear, and automotive parts. description: "PMMA powder (also known as polymethyl methacrylate or acrylic) is bound together using a liquid binder, which hardens after a few seconds. After printing, the parts are hardened in a heat chamber, where the powder is fused together and sandblasted to reduce surface porosity. The resulting part offers a light coarse texture, high level of stiffness, and a low density of 1 g/m^3. Due to the high reusability of the remaining powder, parts can be manufactured more cost-efficiently.",

description: "ULTEM 9085 is a flame-retardant high-performance thermoplastic for digital manufacturing and rapid prototyping. It is ideal for the transportation industry due to its high strength-to-weight ratio and its FST (flame, smoke, and toxicity) rating. ULTEM 9085 allows design and manufacturing engineers to produce fully functional parts that are ideal for advanced functional prototypes or end-use parts without the cost or lead time of traditional tooling. It has a lower resistance to chemicals but is highly retardant to flames (UL94 V-0 compliant).",

description: "SLS PK (polyketone) is an engineering-grade thermoplastic processed via selective laser sintering. Known for its toughness and resistance to fuels, oils, and other hydrocarbons, PK offers stable mechanical properties even in chemically demanding environments. Compared to polyamides, it absorbs significantly less moisture, making it ideal for applications where dimensional stability is critical. In its standard finish, SLS PK parts feature a matte white to off-white color with a slightly grainy surface typical of the process. The combination of durability, chemical resistance, and low moisture uptake makes SLS PK well-suited for functional prototypes and end-use parts in automotive, chemical processing, and industrial equipment.",

description: "Acetal, also known by the brand name Delrin, is a high-performance engineering thermoplastic known for its excellent dimensional stability, low friction, and high stiffness. It machines cleanly with tight tolerances, making it ideal for precision parts. Acetal exhibits good fatigue and wear resistance, making it well-suited for applications involving sliding motion, such as bushings, gears, and bearings. It resists moisture, solvents, and a range of chemicals, while maintaining mechanical integrity in both dry and humid environments. Though not UV stable or flame retardant by default, Acetal is widely used in automotive, industrial, and consumer product applications requiring durability, machinability, and chemical resistance.",

{
id: "77b41b5c-2057-4fa0-ba3d-1ed0665cea79",
name: "PEEK",
featuredImage: "v1754641451/gallery/CNC_milled_PEEK.png",
descriptionShort: "PEEK is a high-strength, heat-resistant thermoplastic with exceptional chemical resistance, wear resistance, and dimensional stability. Ideal for high-performance components in aerospace, automotive, and medical industries.",
description: "PEEK (polyether ether ketone) is a high-performance, engineering-grade thermoplastic known for its exceptional strength, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. It maintains mechanical properties at temperatures up to 250 °C (480 °F), making it ideal for high-temperature applications. PEEK offers high wear resistance, excellent dimensional stability, and is inherently self-lubricating, which reduces the need for additional coatings. It is resistant to a wide range of chemicals, including acids, bases, and organic solvents. Due to these remarkable properties, PEEK is used extensively in demanding industries such as aerospace, automotive, medical devices, and electronics. Components made from PEEK include bearing inserts, gears, seals, valve components, and high-performance insulators. It can also be used in 3D printing and CNC machining for producing precision parts in industrial and medical environments.",

name: "Acrylic (PMMA)",
featuredImage: "v1750690684/gallery/cnc_pmma.png",
descriptionShort: "CNC-milled acrylic offers high clarity, smooth edges, and a glass-like finish. Ideal for displays, covers, and enclosures, it’s precise, weather-resistant, and suited for low-impact uses.",
description: "CNC-milled acrylic (PMMA) is a rigid, transparent thermoplastic known for its excellent optical clarity and smooth surface finish. It is commonly used as a lightweight alternative to glass in applications where transparency, durability, and precision are required. Acrylic machines cleanly, allowing for sharp edges, fine details, and polished surfaces. After milling, parts can be flame polished or buffed to restore optical clarity on edges and faces, though even the standard finish offers a smooth, clean look. Available in clear, tinted, or opaque colors, CNC-milled acrylic is ideal for display components, covers, light guides, and enclosures. It offers good weather resistance and dimensional stability but is more brittle than other plastics, making it better suited for low-impact applications. Its crisp appearance and ease of fabrication make it popular in signage, architecture, and consumer products.",

description: "HDPE is a versatile, high-density thermoplastic known for its excellent impact resistance, low friction, and high chemical resistance. HDPE’s flexibility, dimensional stability, and ability to handle moderate temperatures make it ideal for a variety of industrial applications, including food processing, automotive, medical, and consumer goods. Common uses include bushings, seals, gears, and structural components where wear resistance and low friction are needed, such as in piping systems, marine parts, and packaging. HDPE is easy to machine with good mechanical properties, and it is highly resistant to cracking, abrasion, and corrosion, making it a go-to choice for functional, long-lasting parts.",

name: "Injection Molding Plastics",
featuredImage: "v1730371401/gallery/injection-molded-silicone.webp",
descriptionShort: "Injection molding involves injecting molten plastic into a mold, where it cools and solidifies into a precise shape. Ideal for high-volume production, it ensures consistent quality, detailed designs, and material flexibility across various industries.",
description: "Injection molding is a manufacturing process used to produce plastic parts by injecting molten material into a mold. In this process, plastic granules are fed into a heated barrel, melted, and then injected under high pressure into a precisely designed mold cavity. The molten plastic fills the cavity, taking on the shape of the mold, and is held under pressure until it cools and solidifies. Once hardened, the mold opens, and the finished part is ejected. Injection molding is highly efficient for producing large volumes of parts with consistent quality, tight tolerances, and intricate designs. It supports a variety of plastic materials, enabling flexibility in terms of strength, durability, and appearance. This process is widely used across industries, including automotive, medical, and consumer products, due to its cost-effectiveness for high-volume production and its ability to produce complex geometries and fine details.",

name: "Glass Fiber Polyurethane",
featuredImage: "v1734951058/Vacuum_casting_hero_pckrn2.jpg",
description: "Polyurethane casting resin filled with glass fiber is optimized for vacuum casting of prototypes and short-run production components. By incorporating the glass filler, the resin achieves significantly improved rigidity, dimensional stability, and thermal performance compared to standard unfilled casting resins. The material exhibits low shrinkage, supports tight tolerance reproduction, and maintains good detail fidelity, making it suitable for engineering models, fixtures, functional housings, and components that benefit from added stiffness.
In its standard vacuum-cast finish, GF-PR produces parts with a matte, technical appearance, featuring clean edges and consistent surface texture. While the filler increases structural integrity and heat tolerance, it also reduces ductility relative to unfilled polyurethane systems. This balance makes the material ideal for applications where strength, stability, and repeatability matter more than impact absorption or cosmetic flexibility. This material serves as an effective bridge between prototype and low-volume production, providing a cost-efficient alternative to injection-molded plastics for functional validation.",
descriptionShort: "Polyurethane casting resin filled with glass fiber used for vacuum casting prototypes and low-volume functional parts. The filler blend provides enhanced stiffness, dimensional stability, and heat resistance with a matte, finely textured surface finish.",

name: "PP-Like Polyurethane",
featuredImage: "v1734951058/Vacuum_casting_hero_pckrn2.jpg",
description: "PP-like polyurethane casting resin is an engineering-grade polyurethane casting resin designed for vacuum casting of functional prototypes and low-volume production runs. The material replicates the properties of PP- and HDPE-style thermoplastics, offering a balanced combination of stiffness, toughness, and impact resistance while maintaining dimensional accuracy and stable processing behavior. The material exhibits low shrinkage and reproduces fine geometric details well, making it suitable for housings, covers, and mechanical assemblies that require durable, injection-molded-like performance without the cost of tooling.
In its as-cast state, casting resin parts typically have a smooth, matte surface with a uniform appearance and can be easily machined, painted, dyed, or coated for cosmetic or functional finishing. Its mechanical performance makes it well suited for functional testing, validation, and pre-production where material behavior needs to approximate molded engineering plastics.",

description: "ABS-like Polyurethane is a polyurethane casting resin formulated to simulate the performance and appearance of injection-molded ABS plastics. In vacuum casting, it offers an ideal balance of rigidity, impact toughness, and dimensional accuracy, with low shrinkage and good reproduction of fine geometric features. This makes the material suitable for functional enclosures, covers, housings, ergonomic validation components, snap-fit features, and mechanical assemblies where real-world use and handling are required.
The resin family supports both larger parts and thin-walled geometries. Standard formulations provide reliable filling and curing behavior, while lower-viscosity/longer-flow variants improve detail reproduction and thin-section precision without significantly altering final mechanical characteristics. In the as-cast state, parts typically exhibit a smooth matte or satin surface and are compatible with painting, machining, bonding, drilling, and secondary finishing to match cosmetic or functional production intent.",

name: "PC-Like Polyurethane",
featuredImage: "v1734951058/Vacuum_casting_hero_pckrn2.jpg",
description: "PC-like polyurethane is an engineering-grade casting resin formulated for vacuum-cast prototyping and small-batch production. The material is designed to emulate high-performance thermoplastics with a focus on rigidity, heat resistance, and dimensional stability, making it suitable for applications that require functional validation under mechanical or thermal loading. In its cured state, the material delivers low shrinkage, accurate geometry reproduction, and a smooth matte technical surface that can be post-machined, painted, bonded, or coated as needed for cosmetic or assembly requirements.
Compared to ABS-like systems, PC-like polyurethane leans toward higher stiffness and improved heat performance, which enables use in housings, enclosures, fixtures, covers, structural prototypes, and industrial components that must withstand handling, testing, or pre-production verification. The material bridges the gap between functional prototyping and early production, providing a cost-efficient alternative to injection-molded engineering plastics for automotive, electronics, consumer product, medical device, and industrial design workflows.",
descriptionShort: "PC-like polyurethane casting resin is used in vacuum casting to produce rigid, heat-resistant, and dimensionally stable parts. It is suitable for functional prototypes and low-volume production components that require engineering performance.",

description: "UHMW-PE (Ultra-High Molecular Weight Polyethylene) is an engineering thermoplastic known for its extremely high wear resistance, low friction, and high impact strength. Its properties make it an ideal choice for high-performance applications where parts experience high friction, wear, and harsh environments. It is also commonly used in marine and automotive components. Its self-lubricating nature reduces the need for additional coatings and oils, providing durability in long-term operations.",

Due to its non-reactivity and lubricating properties, PTFE is ideal for sliding and moving components that must withstand wear and exposure to aggressive chemicals.",

In its cured state, PC-like resin exhibits excellent hardness, strong flexural performance, and good resistance to deformation under load, making it suitable for brackets, housings, tooling, fixtures, and mechanical test components. PC-like resin is widely used for applications that require sturdy, injection-molded-like performance, especially where dimensional consistency and mechanical reliability are critical.",
