name: "Ceramic Resin",
featuredImage: "v1764249535/Ceramic_Resin_xs8dk2.png",
descriptionShort: "Ceramic resin is a high-resolution photopolymer that produces rigid parts with excellent stiffness, heat resistance, and dimensional accuracy.",
description: "Ceramic resin is a specialized photopolymer formulated with glass- or ceramic-filled particles, designed to deliver exceptional rigidity, thermal stability, and precision when printed with LCD/MSLA systems. The material cures into a dense, stiff, low-shrink polymer matrix, providing mechanical behavior closer to technical ceramics or fiber-reinforced composites than standard resins. 
Thanks to its high stiffness, low thermal expansion, and resistance to deformation under heat, ceramic resin is well suited for heat-resistant fixtures, molds, tooling, jigs, precision housings, and dimensional test components. Its content enhances both surface hardness and compressive strength, making it ideal for structural applications that require stability and rigidity. Although the material is more brittle than engineering resins, it offers superior accuracy and detail, especially for finely featured or load-bearing shapes. 
Ceramic resin parts may be further post-baked or kiln-fired (depending on the manufacturer) to increase density and ceramic-like performance, though many users rely solely on standard UV post-curing. Overall, ceramic resin combines engineering-grade stiffness, high detail resolution, and heat performance, making it a strong choice for industrial and precision applications requiring ceramic-like behavior from an LCD-printed part.",

description: "In its standard, as-printed state, Ceramic Resin produces parts with a smooth, matte, finely textured surface that reflects the ceramic-filled composition of the material. The cured resin typically appears in a light gray to off-white tone, with a soft, uniform finish and minimal visible layer lines thanks to high-resolution LCD/MSLA printing. Edges, embossed features, and fine geometric details render cleanly, making the material suitable for precision components.
The ceramic content gives the parts a rigid, dense feel with high surface hardness and exceptional dimensional stability. The as-printed finish may show a slightly chalky or stone-like texture, characteristic of ceramic-loaded polymers. This finish does not require post-processing for dimensional accuracy, but the material can be sanded or coated if a smoother or more aesthetic surface is desired.
While extremely stiff and heat resistant, the material is also more brittle than engineering-grade resins, so thin features must be supported appropriately. name: "Anti-Static Resin-ESD",
featuredImage: "v1764249543/ESD_fqo3oq.png",
descriptionShort: "Anti-Static Resin (ESD) produces rigid, high-detail parts with controlled surface resistivity to prevent static buildup. It offers dimensional accuracy, a smooth matte finish, and electrostatic discharge protection for sensitive electronic applications.",
description: "Anti-Static Resin (ESD) is a specialized photopolymer formulated to provide electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection for components used around sensitive electronics. When printed with LCD/MSLA technology, the material produces rigid, high-precision parts with a uniform matte surface and excellent feature resolution. Its formulation incorporates conductive additives that create a controlled surface resistivity range, allowing the finished parts to safely dissipate electrical charges without generating sparks or damaging electronic assemblies.
Despite its conductive properties, the resin maintains strong dimensional stability, low shrinkage, and clean edge definition, making it suitable for housings, jigs, brackets, grippers, trays, sensor mounts, and production tooling used in electronics manufacturing environments.
The material is engineered for mechanical strength, thermal stability, and consistent electrical performance, though it is generally less flexible and slightly more brittle than standard engineering resins due to filler content. Overall, ESD Anti-Static Resin provides a reliable combination of precision, rigidity, and electrostatic protection, making it ideal for functional components in ESD-safe workspaces, automation systems, and electronic assembly workflows.",

name: "Standard",
featuredImage: "v1764249543/ESD_fqo3oq.png",
description: "In its standard, as-printed state, Anti-Static Resin (ESD) produces parts with a uniform matte finish and a dark gray to black appearance. The surface is smooth with fine micro-texture from conductive fillers, giving the part a slightly more grainy feel than standard engineering resins. Thanks to high-resolution LCD/MSLA processing, features such as sharp corners, small embossing, and fine mechanical details render cleanly and accurately with minimal visible layer lines.
The cured material maintains excellent dimensional stability, rigidity, and surface hardness, while offering controlled electrical resistivity in the ESD-safe range (10⁵-10⁷ Ω/sq). This ensures reliable dissipation of static charge without compromising part integrity. While the as-printed surface is visually clean and functional, the material can also be sanded, coated, or precision-finished if required for specific tooling or enclosure needs.
Anti-Static Resin’s standard finish is ideal for electronics housings, jigs, trays, grippers, fixtures, sensor mounts, and components used in ESD-controlled environments. The matte dark surface reflects its functional purpose, providing both a professional appearance and dependable electrostatic protection straight off the printer.",
descriptionShort: "Standard ESD Resin parts feature a smooth, matte surface. The material provides controlled surface resistivity for electrostatic protection, along with strong dimensional accuracy and rigidity suitable for electronics-related applications.",

name: "SLS PEEK",
featuredImage: "v1764249579/PEEK_SLS_avntlh.jpg",
descriptionShort: "SLS PEEK produces exceptionally strong, lightweight parts with outstanding heat resistance, chemical stability, and dimensional accuracy. It delivers near-thermoplastic-molded properties, ideal for aerospace, medical, and industrial applications.",
description: "SLS PEEK (polyether ether ketone) is an ultra-high-performance thermoplastic used to manufacture parts that require exceptional mechanical strength, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. When processed via Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), PEEK yields high-density, precision components with properties comparable to injection-molded PEEK, enabling true end-use manufacturing for critical engineering applications.
As printed, SLS PEEK parts exhibit a light tan to beige matte finish with the fine micro-granular texture characteristic of high-temperature sintering. The material’s inherent stability ensures excellent dimensional accuracy, low creep, and reliable performance under continuous loads. With a heat deflection temperature above 250 °C, superior fatigue resistance, and full chemical inertness, SLS PEEK excels in environments where ordinary polymers fail.
SLS PEEK is widely used for aerospace components, medical instruments, high-temperature housings, bushings, gears, brackets, manifolds, and components exposed to solvents or aggressive chemicals. Its combination of strength-to-weight ratio, biocompatibility (for certain grades), and long-term reliability makes it one of the most capable polymers available for additive manufacturing.",

description: "In its standard, as-printed state, SLS PEEK produces parts with a matte tan to light beige finish and a fine micro-granular texture typical of high-temperature laser sintering. Layer lines are minimal and surfaces appear uniformly powder-textured, giving the material a clean, functional engineering aesthetic. The dense, semi-crystalline structure formed during sintering provides excellent dimensional stability, ensuring that even complex geometries maintain tight tolerances without warping.
SLS PEEK delivers exceptional mechanical performance, including high tensile strength, outstanding stiffness, and superior fatigue and creep resistance. Its extreme heat resistance (HDT > 250 °C) and complete chemical inertness make it suitable for harsh industrial environments where metals or lower-grade polymers may fail. While the as-printed surface is already functional for most uses, it can be further processed through machining, polishing, or coating if smoother finishes or tighter fitting interfaces are required.
Typical applications include aerospace components, medical instrument parts, chemical-exposed housings, high-temperature fixtures, bushings, gears, manifolds, and precision industrial hardware. The standard SLS finish showcases the material’s inherent technical character while delivering unmatched polymer performance directly out of the printer.",

name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1767015331/gallery/polished_SLS_peek.png",
description: "Polished SLS PEEK parts combine the outstanding mechanical and thermal performance of laser-sintered PEEK with an enhanced surface finish achieved through mechanical polishing. The polishing process reduces the inherent powder-based roughness of SLS, resulting in a smoother, semi-matte to satin surface with a more uniform appearance while preserving tight dimensional accuracy. The material typically retains its light tan to beige tone, with softened edges and improved tactile quality.
PEEK is a high-performance thermoplastic known for its excellent strength-to-weight ratio, extreme heat resistance (HDT > 250 °C), chemical inertness, and long-term fatigue resistance. Polishing improves cleanability, wear behavior, and suitability for sliding or mating surfaces, making the material more appropriate for functional interfaces and exposed components. While the surface becomes visually refined, the internal structure and performance of the part remain unchanged.",

The material offers high tensile strength compared to many other plastics, allowing it to perform reliably under mechanical stress and repeated loading.

Nylon 6/6 also provides excellent wear resistance and low friction characteristics, making it particularly suitable for moving components such as bushings, gears, and sliding surfaces. It offers good resistance to oils, fuels, and many industrial chemicals, helping maintain performance in demanding environments.

While Nylon 6/6 can absorb moisture over time, which may slightly affect dimensional stability, it remains highly durable and widely used in engineering applications. Additional finishing processes or stabilization methods may be applied when tighter tolerances or improved environmental resistance are required.",

ULTEM 2300 offers excellent thermal resistance, maintaining mechanical integrity at elevated temperatures and performing reliably in continuous-use environments up to approximately 170 °C. It also provides excellent flame resistance and low smoke emission, making it suitable for safety-critical applications.

In addition, the material offers excellent resistance to creep, deformation, and many industrial chemicals, while maintaining stable electrical insulation properties. descriptionShort: "Flexible TPU is a rubber-like material suitable for functional prototypes and wear-resistant parts.",
description: "Flexible TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) is a standard rubber-like, powder-based material. It is able to bend and twist like rubber (shore hardness 86-90A), but still demonstrates a high level of strength, heat resistance (90-130 °C), and exceptional shock absorption. This makes the material great for functional parts and prototypes with rubber-like properties used in industrial settings. The material is water-resistant but not waterproof and should not be in contact with water over extensive periods of time. The material is 3D printed on industrial grade 3D printers that offer the highest quality, using either Selective Laser Sintering or Multi Jet Fusion printing processes.",

descriptionShort: "FDM printed TPE provides rubber-like flexibility and durability. It is ideal for parts that will be in contact with skin, food or used in resilient environments.",
description: "FDM TPE (Thermoplastic Elastomer) is a versatile 3D printing material known for its rubber-like flexibility and durability. It offers various forms of elasticity, allowing extensive stretching and returning to its original shape, making it ideal for parts like seals, gaskets, and grips. TPE is also suited for applications within the food sector and in medical applications where skin contact is needed. TPE absorbs shocks, resists chemicals and UV light, and is excellent for applications needing high flexibility and resilience.",

name: "Silicone Resin",
featuredImage: "v1765372540/gallery/Silicone_resin.png",
descriptionShort: "Silicone resin for SLA 3D printing produces soft, flexible parts with rubber-like elasticity and durability. It offers excellent rebound, fine detail resolution, and reliable performance for seals, gaskets, and functional flexible prototypes.",
description: "Silicone resin for SLA 3D printing is an advanced, flexible photopolymer engineered to replicate the softness, elasticity, and resilience of molded silicone. When cured, it forms parts with a smooth, matte surface and a distinctly rubber-like feel, capable of bending, stretching, and compressing without cracking or tearing. SLA technology enables high detail accuracy, allowing the material to produce thin features, intricate channels, and complex geometries that are difficult or impossible to manufacture through traditional molding.
This material is ideal for applications requiring flexibility, repeated deformation, and comfort, such as seals, gaskets, damping elements, wearable components, grips, and functional elastomer prototypes. It maintains consistent mechanical performance over many cycles, offering strong rebound and durability under load. Silicone resin provides a practical, rapid alternative to molded silicone by enabling the fabrication of soft, elastomeric parts directly from the printer, offering greater design freedom and faster iteration.",

name: "Standard (Shore A40)",
featuredImage: "v1765372540/gallery/Silicone_resin.png",
description: "In its standard state, Silicone 40A Resin for SLA produces parts with a smooth, matte finish and a distinctly soft, elastic feel that closely resembles molded silicone rubber. The material cures with a slightly translucent or tinted appearance depending on color formulation, and showcases excellent feature definition thanks to the high-resolution capabilities of SLA technology. 
The as-printed components maintain high flexibility, rebound, and resistance to tearing or cracking under repeated bending, making the material ideal for functional elastomeric designs. Its inherent softness and durability allow the creation of complex internal channels, thin walls, and organic shapes that would be difficult to mold conventionally. The standard finish requires no additional processing for most applications, though parts may be cleaned or lightly post-cured to improve stability.
Typical uses include seals, gaskets, soft-touch grips, wearable components, damping features, protective covers, and flexible mechanisms that benefit from elastomeric performance combined with the geometric freedom of SLA printing. The as-printed finish highlights the material’s rubber-like behavior while offering precise, reliable performance for prototyping and end-use applications.",
descriptionShort: "Silicone 40A Resin parts feature a smooth, matte surface with soft, flexible, rubber-like behavior. The material prints with high detail accuracy and produces durable elastomeric components suitable for seals, gaskets, and wearable prototypes.",

name: "Spectroplast® TrueSil",
featuredImage: "v1748332553/gallery/New%20images/silicone_rubber_4_revised.png",
descriptionShort: "TrueSil is a 3D-printable pure silicone offering high flexibility, biocompatibility, and durability. Ideal for seals, wearables, and medical parts, it resists heat, UV, and repeated deformation.",
description: "Spectroplast TrueSil is an industrial-grade, 3D-printable LSR (liquid silicone rubber) known for its exceptional flexibility, biocompatibility, and long-term durability. Unlike thermoplastic elastomers (TPE or TPU), TrueSil elastomers are made of 100% pure silicone and fulfill market standards in terms of performance and surface quality. They maintain stable mechanical properties across a wide temperature range from -50 °C to +200 °C. The material provides excellent elongation at break, rebound elasticity, and resistance to UV, ozone, and aging.
TrueSil is certified for skin and food contact applications (ISO 10993 and USP Class VI), making it suitable for both medical and consumer-grade products. It's frequently used for seals, gaskets, cushioning components, wearable devices, prosthetics, and other parts requiring soft-touch functionality and repeated deformation.",

description: "TrueSil A50 is a mid-range silicone that provides higher stiffness and improved shape retention than A20 or A35, while still maintaining elastomeric performance. A50 is often chosen when a firmer feel and more structural support are required without sacrificing flexibility.",
descriptionShort: "TrueSil A50 delivers firmer, more resilient silicone performance for seals, dampers, and connectors, combining durability with reliable elastic recovery.",

featuredImage: "v1537537314/gallery/flexible_plastic.jpg",
descriptionShort: "SLS TPE is a versatile, flexible material known for its rubber-like elasticity, thermal stability, and chemical resistance. Common applications are hoses, seals, gaskets, footwear, and medical devices.",
description: "SLS TPE (Thermoplastic Elastomer) is a versatile, flexible material known for its rubber-like elasticity and resilience. It combines the advantageous properties of both thermoplastics and elastomers, offering excellent flexibility, impact resistance, and fatigue endurance. TPE exhibits good thermal stability and can withstand a wide range of temperatures, making it suitable for diverse applications. Its chemical resistance to oils, solvents, and various chemicals enhances its durability in challenging environments. TPE is often preferred for its ease of processing and recycling capabilities, contributing to sustainable manufacturing practices. TPE is commonly used in producing flexible hoses, seals, gaskets, footwear, and medical devices, where comfort and adaptability are critical.",

descriptionShort: "TEPU 50A by Inkbit® is a soft, rubber-like polyurethane ideal for flexible parts that need durability and precision. With a Shore hardness of 50A, it’s perfect for seals, cushioning, wearables, and soft robotics.",
description: "TEPU 50A by Inkbit® is a soft, flexible polyurethane material engineered for applications requiring high elasticity and durability. With a Shore hardness of 50A, it offers a rubber-like feel and is ideal for soft-touch parts and components that undergo repeated stress. Printed using Inkbit’s Vision-Controlled Jetting (VCJ) technology, TEPU 50A delivers smooth surfaces and precise detail, even on complex geometries. It combines high elongation, tear resistance, and low compression set, ensuring parts maintain performance under dynamic loads. Suitable for seals, cushioning, wearable devices, and soft robotics, it provides reliable, repeatable results for both prototyping and end-use applications.",

description: "HP® 3D High Reusability TPU 01 is a flexible, durable thermoplastic polyurethane designed for HP Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) 3D printing. It combines high elasticity with excellent impact resistance, enabling parts to bend, compress, or stretch while maintaining structural integrity. The material is ideal for functional prototypes, wearables, gaskets, seals, cushioning elements, and custom components that require both flexibility and strength. TPU 01 is compatible with repeated use in HP MJF workflows and delivers consistent mechanical performance and surface quality across multiple print cycles.",

{
id: "560efbcd-2a33-4a9a-8f37-2f2cedf02ec9",
name: "Vapor Smoothed",
featuredImage: "v1721400238/gallery/TPU_Vapor_Smoothed.png",
description: "When produced with Multi Jet Fusion (MJF), HP® 3D HR TPU 01 naturally has a slightly grainy, matte gray surface. Vapor smoothing transforms this texture by exposing the part to a controlled solvent vapor that reflows and seals the outer layer. The result is a satin-gloss finish that eliminates porosity, darkens the surface to a more uniform gray, and enhances both durability and aesthetics. The process improves resistance to moisture, dirt, and chemicals, while making parts easier to clean. Crucially, TPU 01's intrinsic properties – elasticity, toughness, and tear resistance – remain intact, ensuring that the material continues to perform under repeated flexing and mechanical stress. This makes vapor smoothed MJF TPU 01 especially suitable for seals, gaskets, consumer goods, and industrial applications requiring both flexibility and a refined appearance.",
descriptionShort: "Vapor smoothed MJF HP® 3D HR TPU 01 parts have a sealed, satin-gloss surface with reduced porosity. The finish improves appearance, cleanability, and resistance to moisture while retaining full flexibility.",

id: "5e97ebe5-c075-43d9-b8dc-828dcbd940ea",
name: "Polished",
featuredImage: "v1662650035/gallery/New%20images/Revised/SLS_TPU_polished.jpg",
description: "Polishing MJF HP® 3D HR TPU 01 involves mechanically or chemically refining the surface to reduce the grainy texture of as-printed parts. This process creates a smooth, glossy finish that highlights the material’s natural flexibility and toughness while improving its visual appeal. The polished surface also enhances cleanability and reduces the visibility of dirt and moisture, making it ideal for applications where both performance and aesthetics are important. Despite the surface transformation, the material retains its intrinsic elasticity, tear resistance, and impact strength, ensuring that parts continue to perform reliably under repeated stress. Polished MJF TPU 01 is ideal for seals, gaskets, protective covers, and consumer products that require both a refined look and long-term durability.",
descriptionShort: "Polished MJF HP® 3D HR TPU 01 parts feature a smooth, glossy surface that enhances the material’s flexibility and durability. The polishing process reduces surface texture, improving both aesthetics and cleanability.",

name: "Standard PU Coated",
featuredImage: "gallery/brass_pu_coated.jpg",
description: "Brass is good for jewelry and jewelry prototypes. When polished, brass is smooth and shiny. When unpolished, it is matte, rough and looks antique. Objects will tarnish over time and may need to be polished. It is 3D printed in multiple steps. First, 3D printed in high resolution wax. A mold of liquid plaster is made using the wax model, afterwards injection molded. Brass consists of 15% zinc, 5% tin, and 80% copper. A good rule of thumb is to scale your model up by 1% to allow a natural shrinkage, which occurs during the production process.",
descriptionShort: "Raw brass with a PU coating to slow down oxidation. Slightly smoother than the standard finish.",

description: "Lost wax cast platinum parts exhibit a brilliant silvery-white appearance with a smooth, refined surface that highlights the precision achievable through investment casting. This noble metal offers exceptional strength, density, and resistance to tarnish, oxidation, and chemical wear, making it ideal for applications demanding durability and lasting visual appeal. Platinum’s excellent malleability and biocompatibility also make it well-suited for jewelry, high-end watchmaking, medical instruments, and specialized industrial components. The lost wax casting process enables the creation of highly detailed geometries with fine surface definition, followed by polishing to achieve a mirror-like or satin finish as desired. The result is a component that combines premium aesthetics, precision craftsmanship, and outstanding long-term stability.",

{
id: "e5dd5a61-63c5-4fec-a78c-8c5812208cbf",
name: "Sanded",
featuredImage: "gallery/sanded_pla.jpg",
description: "Flat surfaces, curves and overhangs are smoothed out with specific tools or by manually sanding them to the extent that layer lines are less visible. The color might be slightly uneven due to the sanding. PLA is short for Polylactic Acid, a thermoplastic polymer that is derived from renewable resources. This feature sets it apart from other commonly used plastics. PLA material is great for low cost prototyping, low-wear toys, functional parts under light load, and containers. The printing process - An extruder deposits molten plastic onto a build platform, layer by layer, until the model has been created. The printing process creates visible stepping between layers. The infill percentage can be customized to your needs in the "Finish" step of our configuration.",
descriptionShort: "Smooth sanded finish in various colors.",

descriptionShort: "Made from recycled materials, recycled rPETG offers a sustainable alternative to regular PETG.",
description: "Recycled PETG is derived from the recycling of post-consumer or post-industrial PETG products.
It helps mitigate environmental impacts by reducing the need for new raw materials, conserving energy, and diverting plastics from landfills or incineration.

name: "Titanium Grade 2",

descriptionShort: "Titanium Grade 2 produces lightweight, corrosion-resistant parts with excellent strength and durability. It is ideal for precision components exposed to harsh environments and demanding applications.",
description: "CNC machined Titanium Grade 2 is a commercially pure titanium known for its excellent combination of corrosion resistance, strength, and low weight. It offers reliable mechanical performance while maintaining excellent resistance to chemicals, moisture, and environmental exposure, making it suitable for demanding industrial and structural applications.

Titanium Grade 2 is highly resistant to corrosion, including exposure to saltwater, chemicals, and humid environments. It also offers excellent fatigue resistance and long-term stability, making it well suited for components exposed to repeated stress or harsh operating conditions. Its biocompatibility further enables use in medical and specialized applications.

Typical applications include aerospace components, marine hardware, chemical processing equipment, medical devices, structural parts, and precision mechanical components where corrosion resistance, strength, and weight reduction are critical.",
materialGroupId: "3e3f9707-372f-4f1c-a887-55bd3a3b5cd0",

name: "Standard",
featuredImage: "v1771248091/gallery/CNC_Titanium_Grade_2.png",
description: "In its standard as-machined condition, CNC-machined Titanium Grade 2 exhibits a clean, functional appearance with a uniform matte silver-gray metallic surface and visible machining marks created during the cutting process. The finish reflects precise CNC machining, with sharp edges, accurate geometry, and reliable dimensional accuracy suitable for tight-tolerance assemblies and structural components.

Compared to steel, Titanium Grade 2 offers significantly lower weight while maintaining good strength and excellent durability. Its high fatigue resistance and excellent biocompatibility make it suitable for demanding industrial, marine, aerospace, and medical applications. While the as-machined surface is primarily functional, additional finishing processes such as polishing, bead blasting, or coating can be applied when improved surface appearance or performance is required.

Standard as-machined Titanium Grade 2 parts are ideal for lightweight, corrosion-resistant components requiring precision, durability, and reliable performance in harsh or demanding environments.",
descriptionShort: "Standard as-machined Titanium Grade 2 parts feature a matte silver-gray surface with fine machining marks, offering excellent corrosion resistance, high strength-to-weight ratio, and reliable performance in demanding environments.",

description: "Tricalcium phosphate (TCP) exhibits excellent biocompatibility, bioresorbability, and osteoconductivity, and is therefore a well-established material for bone replacement in regenerative medicine. The material is best used as biological scaffolds, bone substitute implants, and similar applications. The material is non-cytotoxic according to ISO 10993-5 and not irritating to skin as per ISO 10993-10. Certifications available upon request.",

name: "PVA",
featuredImage: "v1768907435/gallery/PVA_supports2.jpg",
descriptionShort: "PVA is a water-soluble thermoplastic used primarily as support material in FDM printing. It dissolves cleanly in water, enabling complex geometries, internal channels, and delicate details that would be difficult or impossible with breakaway support.",
description: "PVA (Polyvinyl Alcohol) is a water-soluble thermoplastic widely used in FDM 3D printing as a dissolvable support material. Its key advantage is the ability to fully dissolve in water, allowing intricate part features such as internal channels, undercuts, thin structures, and complex overhangs to be produced with ease. PVA adheres well to common build materials such as PLA (and in some cases PETG or nylon blends, depending on formulation), making it effective for systems that rely on soluble support strategies. Once printing is complete, the support structure is removed by submerging the part in water, leaving a clean surface finish and preserving fine details without mechanical removal.
PVA itself is not typically used as a structural material due to its low mechanical strength and sensitivity to moisture, but as a soluble support it significantly expands the geometric freedom of FDM printing, making it valuable for engineering prototypes, functional assemblies, and complex hobbyist models alike.",

name: "Standard",
featuredImage: "v1768907435/gallery/PVA_supports2.jpg",
description: "In its standard, as-printed condition, FDM PVA (Polyvinyl Alcohol) produces parts with a matte, slightly textured finish and visible extrusion layer lines. The natural color is typically a warm off-white to pale yellow tone, characteristic of the polymer. While the surface quality is practical and functional, it is not intended for cosmetic applications.
PVA is water-soluble, making it valuable as a dissolvable support material for multi-material FDM printing. After printing, models can be submerged in water to remove internal or external supports, enabling complex geometries, overhangs, undercuts, and internal channels that would be difficult or impossible with mechanical breakaway supports. Although it can be printed as a standalone material, PVA is not typically used for structural components due to its low mechanical strength and sensitivity to moisture.
Standard FDM PVA prints are most commonly used in combination with materials such as PLA and PETG, supporting prototyping, educational models, visual parts, and functional assemblies that require clean internal features or intricate structures. The standard finish provides a straightforward, soluble solution for enhancing the geometric capabilities of FDM 3D printing.",
descriptionShort: "Standard FDM PVA prints feature a matte, off-white surface with visible layer lines. The material is water-soluble and primarily used as dissolvable support for complex geometries.",
